subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R→R and g: R→R are defined by f(x) = 4x − 1 and g(x) = x² + 2, find (gof)(x).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.10, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 12(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to substituting f(x) into g in the right order and one to the expansion, because the order of composition and the squaring of a bracket are the two separate skills being tested. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (gof)(x) — which function acts first, and how you expand what is left.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Put f(x) into g
steps.margin_note: First mark. Keep 4x − 1 inside a bracket when it enters g, so the squaring applies to the whole of it.
steps.memory_tip: In gof, f is inside. Substitute the whole of f(x) wherever g has an x.

recall.must_convey: That in gof the inner function is f, so 4x − 1 is substituted into g, giving (4x − 1)² + 2.
accept: in g o f the inner function is f so four x minus one goes into g
g of four x minus one is four x minus one whole squared plus two
f acts first because it is written second
modata f apply chestham so four x minus one ni g lo pedatham
substitute four x minus one for x in g

steps.why: In gof the function written on the right acts first, so f's output becomes g's input. Writing g(4x − 1) with the bracket kept whole is what makes the next line correct.
common_mistakes: Applying g first, which computes (fog)(x) = 4x² + 7 instead.
Writing g(4x − 1) as 4x − 1 + 2, forgetting that g squares its input.

steps.label: Expand and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand the square into three terms, then add the 2 that belongs to g. The constant 3 is 1 + 2.
steps.memory_tip: (4x − 1)² = 16x² − 2(4x)(1) + 1. The middle term −8x is the one students drop.

recall.must_convey: That (4x − 1)² expands to 16x² − 8x + 1, and adding 2 gives 16x² − 8x + 3.
accept: four x minus one squared is sixteen x squared minus eight x plus one
add two to get sixteen x squared minus eight x plus three
the answer is sixteen x squared minus eight x plus three
expand chesi two add chesthe sixteen x squared minus eight x plus three
the constant is one plus two which is three

steps.why: (4x − 1)² is one bracket squared, so it has three terms, and the middle term comes from twice the product of 4x and 1. The 2 that g adds is added after the expansion, giving the constant 3.
common_mistakes: Writing (4x − 1)² as 16x² − 1 or as 16x² + 1, losing the middle term.
Adding the 2 inside the square and writing (4x + 1)².
